title: Assembling the finite projective-line adjunction from supplied diagonal integrals
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, $N>0$ annihilating $\Lambda$, and work on the ordinary unbounded etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Suppose given a transport $t$ of the concrete finite-root line [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows], a family $d_T$ of normalized projective-line Kummer splittings for every $N$-invertible scheme $T$, its canonical exchange/base-change equations, and the two supported diagonal integral-one identities for each $T$, exactly as specified by ArbitraryBaseFiniteP1Splitting, ArbitraryBaseFiniteP1BaseChange, and finiteP1DiagonalProperty in [lem-sp-tower-p1-arbitrary-base-integrals]. For any scheme $S$ with $N$ invertible, put $P=\mathbf P(\operatorname{Option}(\operatorname{ULift}(\operatorname{Fin}(1)));S)$ and $q:P\to S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Then $Rq_*$ admits right adjoint $K\mapsto(q^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda(\mu_{N,P}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}\Lambda_P))[2]$, with [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist] and [def-kun-derived-tensor]. There is no abstract Tate datum, Noetherian, boundedness or constructibility hypothesis.

source.place: Assembling the finite projective-line adjunction from supplied diagonal integrals; refinement of lem-normalized-projective-line-adjunction proof step 1 or 2.

proof.text: Apply finiteP1CoordinateKernel to the supplied family, base-change and integral hypotheses. This supplies a trace-diagonal datum k and coefficient identification e for the required Option-coordinate projective line, satisfying both canonical integral equations.

Map invertibility of N from global sections to each stalk. The primitive-root trivialization gives an etale cover on which the concrete finite line on S is the constant A-sheaf, exactly the lisse-rank-one hypothesis.

Apply SfDiagonalKernel.triangles to k, the finite line on S, its lisse-rank-one proof, n=1, e and the two integrals. The resulting equations are the left_triangle_components and right_triangle_components fields of Adjunction; the unit and counit fields are the existing canonical SfDiagonalKernel maps. This constructs the adjunction for Rq! and B tensor q*.

The projective-line projection is proper, so transport the left adjoint along the canonical Rq! ≅ Rq* comparison. On the right, apply canonical tensor symmetry to get q*(-) tensor B and derivedTensorRightShiftIso to move the even shift two outside right tensor. Whisker these natural isomorphisms by q*, and apply Adjunction.ofNatIsoRight.

proof_origin.place: Explicit assembly from the existing general diagonal-kernel triangle theorem, followed by properness, canonical tensor symmetry and shift transport.

theorem nonempty_finiteP1AdjunctionOfIntegrals
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hΛ : (N : Λ) = 0)
    (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport Λ N hΛ)
    (d : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (hT : IsUnit (N : Γ(T, ⊤))),
      ArbitraryBaseFiniteP1Splitting Λ N hΛ t T hT)
    (hbc : ArbitraryBaseFiniteP1BaseChange Λ N hΛ t d)
    (hi : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (hT : IsUnit (N : Γ(T, ⊤))),
      finiteP1DiagonalProperty Λ N hΛ t d T hT)
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : IsUnit (N : Γ(S, ⊤))) :
    Nonempty (R((ℙ(Option (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)); S) ↘ S)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ]) ⊣
      L((ℙ(Option (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)); S) ↘ S)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ]) ⋙
        ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)
          ℙ(Option (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)); S)).flip.obj
            ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
              (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateLine ℙ(Option (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)); S) N Λ hΛ)) ⋙
          shiftFunctor _ (2 : ℤ)))
